text: My education and qualifications are: I am honored to serve on the Alameda Unified School District Board of Education because I believe every child deserves an excellent education that prepares them for college, careers, and a fulfilling life. I am proud to put my 25 years of education policy and fiscal expertise to work for the community my family calls home and where my children have attended school. I hold a master’s degree from Harvard Graduate School of Education, and my professional career has focused on strengthening public schools and improving outcomes, particularly for historically underserved students. I previously served as Co-Executive Director of a California-based education advocacy organization, and today, as a Partner with a leading national nonprofit, I help education leaders develop data-driven policies and strategies that support student success. Here in Alameda, I have served as a School Site Council member, chaired the district’s Parcel Tax Oversight Committee, and now serve as an AUSD Trustee. As your board member, I helped secure a 10% pay increase and more affordable health benefits for our educators and staff while advancing a plan for long-term fiscal sustainability. I have also worked to raise academic expectations and expand opportunities for all students. I would be honored to earn your vote and continue serving Alameda’s students, families, and schools.

text:
Professor, Retired Non-Profit Co-founder for a Local Basketball Club
My education and qualifications are: Since joining the AUSD Board, I have actively sought the input of our students, teachers, staff, parents, and community members to meet the challenge of providing our children with the highest quality education. Recognizing the importance of preparing our students to be college and career ready, I established a joint subcommittee between AUSD and Peralta Community College to strengthen our collaboration in offering free services directly to our students. The board has worked closely with stakeholders to pass multiple parcel taxes and facility bonds, ensuring Alameda remains a destination district that retains and attracts excellent teachers and staff. While other districts have suffered staff reductions and budget cuts, our district achieved a three-year labor agreement with our certificated and classified staff—a remarkable accomplishment that reflects the positive, productive working relationships between the board and our labor partners. As a proud Asian-American Alamedan, I attended Otis Elementary School, Lincoln Middle School, and both Alameda High School and Encinal High School. I have earned Accounting, Finance, and Business degrees from the University of California, Berkeley, and Arizona State University. Currently, I serve on the Community of Harbor Bay Isle board, representing my neighborhood. It has been a genuine privilege to serve as your trustee these past four years, and I respectfully ask for your vote. www.gary4alamedakids.com

text: My education and qualifications are: As a parent, community organizer, Peralta College certified Early Childhood Educator (ECE), special needs nanny, and disability rights advocate, I have dedicated my life to serving children and their families. I have one child who graduated from AUSD with an IEP, and another currently enrolled with a 504 Plan.As a former wheelchair youth athlete, I experienced firsthand the challenges many students and families continue to face today. At age 15, I became the lead plaintiff in Putnam v. Oakland Unified School District, by permanently establishing accessibility as a fundamental civil rights issue while uncovering systemic multimillion-dollar bond misappropriation. I will advocate for strong education services for all, accessible learning environments, responsible stewardship of taxpayer dollars, and transparent, accountable decision-making. Our educators deserve the resources and support they need to help every student succeed. As your trustee, I will be your advocate. I will demand independent financial audits of bond allocations, prioritize basic classroom safety, support competitive teacher compensation, and firmly reject campus hate speech. We must invest in every student and educator, so families want to stay and return to Alameda. I respectfully ask for your vote to ensure true public service.

text:
My education and qualifications are: I am a Certified Public Accountant, parent of Alameda Unified School District graduates, and longtime Alameda school volunteer with 20 years of service to Alameda Unified School District. I have served as PTA Treasurer, School Site Council member, and chair of the Alameda Unified School District Parcel Tax Oversight Committee. Professionally, I have more than 25 years of experience in strategic financial planning, budgeting, audits, and financial accountability as a nonprofit Chief Financial Officer, including leadership in affordable housing organizations. As a school board member, my priorities are excellent academic outcomes for every student, responsible budgeting that puts classrooms first, supporting and retaining excellent teachers, safe and welcoming schools, and transparent communication with families and the community. I believe students learn best when schools provide high academic expectations, early support for struggling learners, and opportunities for every child to succeed. I am committed to asking thoughtful questions, listening to families and educators, making data-informed decisions, and ensuring taxpayer dollars are managed responsibly. I have built my career on integrity, collaboration, and accountability. I will bring financial expertise, thoughtful leadership, and a proven record of community service to help Alameda Unified School District provide an excellent education for every student. text: My education and qualifications are: Artificial intelligence is reshaping public education, bringing tremendous opportunities and legitimate concerns. As a former Alameda Board of Education member for 12 years, I believe AI should be governed thoughtfully so our students benefit from personalized learning while schools protect privacy, promote equity, preserve meaningful human relationships, and teach responsible AI use. Technology should empower great teachers—not replace them—and every decision should put students, educators, and families first. As a 45-year Alameda resident, I understand our community’s values, traditions, and educational priorities. My son and two daughters graduated from Alameda public schools, and today five of my grandchildren are continuing that tradition. I want every Alameda student to have the same opportunities my own family has enjoyed through our public schools. Strong schools begin with excellent teachers, responsible governance, and meaningful partnerships with families. Together, we can ensure Alameda’s schools continue to prepare every student to thrive in a rapidly changing world. I would be honored to earn your trust and your vote.
